mathlib_declarations.name: AbsoluteValue
mathlib_declarations.notes: Bundled structure for absolute values on a semiring R mapping to an ordered semiring S. Satisfies nonneg, eq_zero iff zero, mul_map, and triangle inequality.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsNonarchimedean
mathlib_declarations.notes: Predicate `IsNonarchimedean f` for the strong triangle inequality f(a+b) ≤ max(f a, f b).

items.notes: AbsoluteValue covers both archimedean and non-archimedean cases; IsNonarchimedean captures the extra condition.

mathlib_declarations.name: AbsoluteValue.abs
mathlib_declarations.notes: Standard absolute value on a linear ordered field.

mathlib_declarations.name: AbsoluteValue.trivial
mathlib_declarations.notes: The trivial absolute value (0 ↦ 0, else 1).

mathlib_declarations.name: Rat.AbsoluteValue.padic
mathlib_declarations.notes: The p-adic absolute value on ℚ as an AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ.

items.notes: Examples of absolute values: standard |·|_∞, trivial, and p-adic.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsNonarchimedean.apply_natCast_le_one_of_isNonarchimedean
mathlib_declarations.notes: Forward direction: if f is nonarchimedean with f 1 = 1 then f (n : ℕ) ≤ 1 for all n.

mathlib_declarations.name: AbsoluteValue.IsNontrivial
mathlib_declarations.notes: Used in Ostrowski's theorem; the bounded-on-naturals condition appears in the proof.

items.notes: The forward direction (non-arch ⟹ |n|≤1 for all n) is in Mathlib. The converse (|n|≤1 for all n ⟹ non-arch) appears implicitly in Ostrowski's proof but is not a standalone lemma. Needs to be formalized here.

mathlib_declarations.name: CharP.cast_eq_zero_iff
mathlib_declarations.notes: Character of a ring; used to show n · 1 = 0 in positive characteristic.

items.notes: The corollary (positive characteristic ⟹ all absolute values non-archimedean; finite field ⟹ only trivial absolute value) does not have a direct Mathlib theorem. Follows from 01.04.Lemma + CharP facts. Needs to be formalized here.

mathlib_declarations.name: AbsoluteValue.IsEquiv
mathlib_declarations.notes: Two absolute values are equivalent if one is a positive real power of the other.

items.notes: IsEquiv formalizes the equivalence relation on absolute values.
Section introduction. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: padicValNat
mathlib_declarations.notes: p-adic valuation on ℕ: padicValNat p n is the exponent of p in n.

mathlib_declarations.name: padicValInt
mathlib_declarations.notes: p-adic valuation on ℤ.

mathlib_declarations.name: padicValRat
mathlib_declarations.notes: p-adic valuation on ℚ (as an integer-valued function).

mathlib_declarations.name: padicNorm
mathlib_declarations.notes: The p-adic absolute value |x|_p = p^(-v_p(x)) on ℚ.

mathlib_declarations.name: Rat.AbsoluteValue.padic
mathlib_declarations.notes: The p-adic absolute value packaged as AbsoluteValue ℚ ℝ.

items.notes: Full Mathlib coverage of the p-adic valuation and absolute value on ℚ.

mathlib_declarations.name: Rat.AbsoluteValue.equiv_real_or_padic
mathlib_declarations.notes: Ostrowski's theorem: every nontrivial absolute value on ℚ is equivalent to |·|_∞ or |·|_p for some prime p.

items.notes: Ostrowski's theorem is fully proved in Mathlib for ℚ.

mathlib_declarations.name: NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one
mathlib_declarations.notes: Product formula for number fields: for nonzero x in K, the product over all places of the normalized absolute value |x|_v equals 1.

items.notes: The product formula for ℚ is a special case of the number field product formula. The lecture statement (∏_{p≤∞} |x|_p = 1 for x ∈ ℚ×) follows directly.
Section introduction. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: Valuation
mathlib_declarations.notes: Structure for valuations: ring homomorphism k× → Γ₀ satisfying v(x+y) ≥ min(v(x),v(y)). Discrete valuations use Γ₀ = ℤ with WithTop.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing
mathlib_declarations.notes: Class for DVRs: local PID that is not a field.

mathlib_declarations.name: Valuation.integer
mathlib_declarations.notes: The valuation ring {x : k | v(x) ≥ 0} of a valuation v on a field k.

items.notes: Valuation and DVR are both fully covered in Mathlib.
Discussion text explaining connection between valuations and absolute values. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: ValuationRing
mathlib_declarations.notes: Class: integral domain where for any pair of elements, one divides the other (equivalently: for all x in FracField, x ∈ A or x⁻¹ ∈ A).

mathlib_declarations.name: PreValuationRing
mathlib_declarations.notes: Weaker version without domain assumption.

items.notes: ValuationRing matches the lecture definition (A is a valuation ring iff for all x ∈ K, x ∈ A or x⁻¹ ∈ A).
Discussion text. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsLocalRing
mathlib_declarations.notes: Class: nontrivial ring where for every a, either a or 1-a is a unit. Equivalent to having a unique maximal ideal.

items.notes: Local ring is fully covered.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsLocalRing.ResidueField
mathlib_declarations.notes: Definition: R ⧸ maximalIdeal R as a field.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsLocalRing.residue
mathlib_declarations.notes: The quotient map R →+* ResidueField R.

items.notes: Residue field is fully covered.
Discussion text. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: Localization.AtPrime
mathlib_declarations.notes: The localization of ℤ at a prime ideal (p), giving ℤ_(p) = {a/b : p ∤ b}.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsLocalRing.ResidueField
mathlib_declarations.notes: The residue field of ℤ_(p) is ℤ/pℤ ≅ 𝔽_p.

items.notes: The construction of ℤ_(p) as a localization is in Mathlib; the identification of maximal ideal as (p) and residue field as 𝔽_p needs to be made explicit.

mathlib_declarations.name: PowerSeries
mathlib_declarations.notes: Formal power series ring k[[t]].

mathlib_declarations.name: LaurentSeries
mathlib_declarations.notes: Laurent series field k((t)) = fraction field of k[[t]].

mathlib_declarations.name: PowerSeries.order
mathlib_declarations.notes: Order of vanishing at 0 for a power series; gives the t-adic valuation.

items.notes: Basic constructions are in Mathlib. The specific valuation on k((t)) with value group ℤ and valuation ring k[[t]] can be assembled from these pieces.
Section introduction. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing
mathlib_declarations.notes: The DVR class in Mathlib is defined as: local PID that is not a field.

mathlib_declarations.name: DiscreteValuationRing.iff_pid_with_one_nonzero_prime
mathlib_declarations.notes: DVR iff PID with unique nonzero prime ideal.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsDedekindDomain.isDVR_of_onlyOnePrime
mathlib_declarations.notes: Characterizes DVRs among Dedekind domains (noetherian integrally closed dim ≤ 1).

items.notes: Several of the equivalences in Theorem 1.16 are provable from Mathlib. The full 7-way equivalence stated in the lecture needs to be assembled from multiple Mathlib lemmas.
Section introduction. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsIntegral
mathlib_declarations.notes: Predicate: IsIntegral R x holds if x is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in R.

mathlib_declarations.name: Algebra.IsIntegral
mathlib_declarations.notes: Class: all elements of an algebra are integral.

items.notes: Full Mathlib coverage.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsIntegral.add
mathlib_declarations.notes: If x and y are integral over R, then x + y is integral over R.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsIntegral.mul
mathlib_declarations.notes: If x and y are integral over R, then x * y is integral over R.

items.notes: The lecture proof uses algebraic closure and symmetric polynomials (external deps); Mathlib's proofs are self-contained and direct.

mathlib_declarations.name: integralClosure
mathlib_declarations.notes: The integral closure of R in A: subalgebra of all elements of A that are integral over R.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsIntegrallyClosed
mathlib_declarations.notes: Predicate: R is integrally closed in its fraction field (all elements of Frac(R) integral over R lie in R).

items.notes: Full Mathlib coverage.

mathlib_declarations.name: Algebra.IsIntegral.trans
mathlib_declarations.notes: If B is integral over A and C is integral over B, then C is integral over A (transitivity of integrality).

items.notes: Transitivity of integrality is fully in Mathlib.

mathlib_declarations.name: integralClosure.isIntegrallyClosedOfFiniteExtension
mathlib_declarations.notes: The integral closure of R in a finite extension L is integrally closed in L.

items.notes: The corollary (integral closure is integrally closed) is in Mathlib.

mathlib_declarations.name: GCDMonoid.toIsIntegrallyClosed
mathlib_declarations.notes: Every GCD monoid (in particular every UFD, and hence every PID, and hence ℤ) is integrally closed.

mathlib_declarations.name: Int.instIsIntegrallyClosed
mathlib_declarations.notes: Instance: ℤ is integrally closed (derived from GCDMonoid).

items.notes: ℤ is a GCDMonoid in Mathlib, so IsIntegrallyClosed ℤ follows automatically. The lecture proves it directly using the rational root test.

mathlib_declarations.name: GCDMonoid.toIsIntegrallyClosed
mathlib_declarations.notes: Every GCDMonoid (which includes all UFDs) is integrally closed.

mathlib_declarations.name: UniqueFactorizationMonoid.instGCDMonoid
mathlib_declarations.notes: Every UFD is a GCDMonoid.

items.notes: UFD ⟹ integrally closed follows from these two instances.
Counterexample showing ℤ[√5] is not integrally closed (since (1+√5)/2 is integral over ℤ but not in ℤ[√5]). No direct Mathlib coverage; needs concrete computation.
Discussion text. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: Valuation.isIntegrallyClosed
mathlib_declarations.notes: The valuation ring of a valuation is integrally closed.

mathlib_declarations.name: Valuation.isIntegrallyClosed_integers
mathlib_declarations.notes: Instance: the integer ring (valuation ring) of a valuation is integrally closed.

items.notes: Full Mathlib coverage.

mathlib_declarations.name: NumberField
mathlib_declarations.notes: Class: a field K with CharZero and [FiniteDimensional ℚ K] — i.e. a finite extension of ℚ.

mathlib_declarations.name: RingOfIntegers
mathlib_declarations.notes: Definition: 𝓞 K = integralClosure ℤ K, the ring of integers of the number field K.

items.notes: Number fields and their rings of integers are fully covered in Mathlib.

mathlib_declarations.name: NumberField.RingOfIntegers.isIntegrallyClosed
mathlib_declarations.notes: 𝓞 K is integrally closed in K.

items.notes: The remark discusses 𝒪_K as the maximal order (free ℤ-module of rank [K:ℚ]). The finiteness/freeness of 𝒪_K as a ℤ-module is in Mathlib. The 'order' concept (sub-ℤ-algebra that is a free ℤ-module of rank n) is not a standalone Mathlib type.

mathlib_declarations.name: minpoly.isIntegrallyClosed_eq_field_fractions
mathlib_declarations.notes: For integrally closed R, if s is integral over R and K = Frac(R), then minpoly K s = (minpoly R s).map (algebraMap R K).

mathlib_declarations.name: IsIntegrallyClosed.isIntegral_iff_leadingCoeff_dvd
mathlib_declarations.notes: For integrally closed R with fraction field K, x ∈ L is integral over R iff the minimal polynomial of x over K has coefficients in R.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsIntegrallyClosed.minpoly.unique
mathlib_declarations.notes: Characterizes the minimal polynomial over an integrally closed ring.

items.notes: The key result (α integral over A iff min poly ∈ A[x]) is covered by these lemmas.
Computation showing (1+√7)/2 has minimal polynomial x² - x - 3/2 ∉ ℤ[x], hence not integral over ℤ. No direct Mathlib coverage; needs a concrete computation.
Reference list. No formalizable content.

mathlib_declarations.name: Nat.factorization_prod_pow_eq_self
mathlib_declarations.notes: Every natural number equals the product of its prime factors.

mathlib_declarations.name: LaurentSeries

mathlib_declarations.name: PowerSeries.order
mathlib_declarations.notes: Order of vanishing (the t-adic valuation).

mathlib_declarations.name: minpoly
mathlib_declarations.notes: The minimal polynomial of an algebraic element x over a ring R: monic, irreducible (over fields), and x is a root.

mathlib_declarations.name: AlgebraicClosure
mathlib_declarations.notes: Algebraic closure of a field: every polynomial splits completely.

mathlib_declarations.name: IsAlgClosed
mathlib_declarations.notes: Class: algebraically closed field.

mathlib_declarations.name: MvPolynomial.IsSymmetric
mathlib_declarations.notes: Symmetric polynomial predicate.

mathlib_declarations.name: Polynomial.resultant
mathlib_declarations.notes: Resultant of two polynomials.

external_deps.notes: Symmetric polynomials and resultants are in Mathlib. The specific use in Prop 1.18 (the product ∏(z - (α_i + β_j)) has integer coefficients) can likely be assembled from these. Mathlib's proof of IsIntegral.add doesn't use this approach directly.

mathlib_declarations.name: Algebra.IsIntegral.trans
mathlib_declarations.notes: If B is integral over A and C is integral over B then C is integral over A.

external_deps.notes: Full Mathlib coverage (this is the result the lecture defers to [1] and [2]).

mathlib_declarations.name: Padic
mathlib_declarations.notes: The p-adic numbers ℚ_p as a field completion.

mathlib_declarations.name: UniformSpace.Completion
mathlib_declarations.notes: Abstract completion of a uniform space.

external_deps.notes: ℚ_p is fully in Mathlib. General local fields (completions of global fields) and their theory are less developed. The p-adic integers ℤ_p as a DVR/local ring is available.

mathlib_declarations.name: FunctionField
mathlib_declarations.notes: Function fields over finite fields F_q(t) are in Mathlib.

external_deps.notes: Function fields over finite fields are in Mathlib. The general theory of global fields (as a unification of number fields and function fields) is partial.

mathlib_declarations.name: Polynomial.isInteger_of_is_root_of_monic
mathlib_declarations.notes: If r/s (in lowest terms) is a root of a monic integer polynomial, then s = ±1 (i.e. the root is actually an integer).

mathlib_declarations.name: Polynomial.isLocalization_rat_root
mathlib_declarations.notes: Rational root theorem for PIDs.

external_deps.notes: The rational root theorem is in Mathlib.
